example.question: The line $l$ has equation $x + 2y = 7$. The line $k$ has equation $3x - 2y = 5$. Find the point where $l$ and $k$ cross.

steps.say: The $y$ terms are $+2y$ and $-2y$. Add the two equations and they cancel.
Put $\hl{2}{x = 3}$ into the equation of $l$ and solve for $y$.
The point must also be on $k$. Put both values into $3x - 2y$.

title: Use slopes to show/construct parallel and perpendicular lines
show: line 2x+3y-6=0 and the perpendicular line through P(4,1) with right-angle mark

example.question: The line $l$ has equation $2x + 3y - 6 = 0$. The line $k$ passes through $P(4, 1)$ and is perpendicular to $l$. Find the equation of $k$.

steps.say: Make $y$ the subject to read off the slope.
Perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$. Turn $\hl{1}{-\frac{2}{3}}$ upside down and change the sign.
Use the slope $\hl{2}{\frac{3}{2}}$ and the point $P(4, 1)$ in $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$.
Multiply by $2$ to clear the fraction, then move every term to one side.

title: Interpret a linear relationship in context
show: straight line C=40+25x style cost graph with the y-intercept (call-out fee) and the slope (hourly rate) marked

example.question:
A plumber charges a call-out fee plus an hourly rate. The cost, in euro, of a job lasting $x$ hours is $C = 40 + 30x$.
(i) What do $40$ and $30$ mean?
(ii) A job costs $190$ euro. How many hours did it last?

steps.say: The number with $x$ is the slope. The number on its own is the start value.

rows.aside: The slope is $\hl{1}{30}$: the cost goes up $30$ euro for each extra hour.
The start value is $\hl{2}{40}$: the cost at $x = 0$, the call-out fee.

steps.say: The job costs $\hl{4}{190}$ euro. Put that in for $C$.
Take away the start value $\hl{2}{40}$ first. Then divide by the slope $\hl{1}{30}$.

title: Find the area of a triangle from vertices
show: triangle A(3,2), B(7,5), C(5,9) on a grid, maybe with enclosing rectangle

example.question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A(3, 2)$, $B(7, 5)$ and $C(5, 9)$.

steps.say: Slide the whole triangle so that $A$ lands on $(0, 0)$. Take $3$ from every $x$ and $2$ from every $y$.
Call the new points $(x_1, y_1) = \hl{1}{(4, 3)}$ and $(x_2, y_2) = \hl{2}{(2, 7)}$. Put them into the area formula.
Do the multiplications first. The bars mean the answer is never negative.

title: Divide a segment internally in a ratio
show: A(-3,4) and B(7,-1) with P dividing AB in ratio 2:3 marked on the segment

example.question: The points are $A(-3, 4)$ and $B(7, -1)$. The point $P$ lies on $[AB]$ so that $|AP| : |PB| = 2 : 3$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

steps.say: Here $m : n = 2 : 3$, $(x_1, y_1) = (-3, 4)$ and $(x_2, y_2) = (7, -1)$. The formula is $\left(\dfrac{nx_1 + mx_2}{m + n},\ \dfrac{ny_1 + my_2}{m + n}\right)$.

rows.aside: $P$ is closer to $A$, because its part of the ratio is the smaller one.

steps.say: Put the $x$ values and the ratio into the formula.
Do the same with the $y$ values.

title: Find the perpendicular distance from a point to a line
show: point P(1,-2) and line y=3x/4+2 with the perpendicular from P to the line marked with right angle

example.question: Find the perpendicular distance from the point $P(1, -2)$ to the line $y = \frac{3}{4}x + 2$.

steps.say: The formula needs the line as $ax + by + c = 0$. Multiply every term by $4$ to clear the fraction, then move everything to one side.
Put $a$, $b$, $c$ and the point $(x_1, y_1) = (1, -2)$ into the distance formula.
Work out the top first and keep it positive, because the bars mean size. Then the square root underneath.
